ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 5 — Sick Visit — Mahalia Jackson

code.originalText: Same-day sick visit for laryngitis on immunosuppressive treatment

text.paragraph: Hoarse voice and sore throat for three days, with a concert in four days. [S]

Ms. Jackson called on Monday and was seen the same day. A cold began five days ago, after a weekend of two concerts and a church service; for three days her voice has been hoarse and breaks on high notes, her throat is sore, and she has a mild dry cough. Her highest temperature at home was 37.5 °C. She has no breathlessness beyond her usual, no chest pain, no palpitations, and no shocks from her defibrillator. She takes prednisone 20 mg each morning, methotrexate 20 mg on Sundays with folic acid daily, atovaquone, metoprolol, alendronate and vitamin D, and has missed no doses. She has a concert on Friday and is worried about singing through it. She has had no thoughts of self-harm. [S]

Vital signs recorded on 2026-06-15; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well; hoarse, breathy voice; temperature 37.4 °C, pulse 72, blood pressure 134/84, oxygen saturation 97 percent on room air
Head, eyes, ears, nose, and throat
Mildly red throat without exudate; no thrush on the tongue, palate or throat; clear nasal discharge; ear drums normal
No tender or enlarged nodes; no stridor
Clear to auscultation; no crackles or wheeze

Breathlessness on exertion and a dry cough for three months, worse on tour, with tiredness and chest tightness; she can no longer hold long phrases; bilateral hilar lymph node enlargement on today's chest radiograph; granulomas were reported at an abdominal operation twelve years ago, with no pathology report available: sarcoidosis must be confirmed by tissue and other causes excluded
S — Synthetic presenting problem anchored to the documented breathlessness during performances and the 1952 granulomas. Superseded by the tissue diagnosis at the consultation.

Palpitations with two spells of light-headedness while singing; ECG today: sinus rhythm with first-degree atrioventricular block (PR 240 ms) and frequent ventricular ectopic beats: cardiac involvement must be looked for
S — Synthetic finding; superseded when cardiac sarcoidosis was diagnosed.
Hypercalcemia: calcium 10.8 mg/dL with a high 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D and a low 25-hydroxyvitamin D, while taking an over-the-counter calcium and vitamin D supplement; creatinine slightly raised
S — Synthetic finding; resolved on treatment.

Pulmonary sarcoidosis with hilar and mediastinal lymph node involvement (Scadding stage II), confirmed by non-necrotizing granulomas on EBUS-guided lymph node aspiration with negative stains and cultures; mild restriction and reduced diffusing capacity; synthetic modern detail linked to her documented sarcoidosis
S — Synthetic histology, stage and lung function; her biographer reports a diagnosis of sarcoidosis after granulomas were found at an operation (D, probable).

Acute viral laryngitis: three days of hoarseness, a sore throat and a mild dry cough after a cold, without fever, on prednisone 20 mg and methotrexate; rapid influenza and COVID-19 tests negative; no thrush; resolved
S — Synthetic acute infection; not a historical claim.

Cardiac sarcoidosis: first-degree atrioventricular block, ventricular ectopy (6 percent of beats) with nonsustained ventricular tachycardia, left ventricular ejection fraction 47 percent, patchy late gadolinium enhancement of the basal septum and inferolateral wall, and matching focal FDG uptake on PET; synthetic modern detail linked to the documented private account that sarcoidosis was in her heart
S — Synthetic cardiac findings; the account that her doctors told her sarcoidosis was in her heart rests on her biographer (D, probable), and the interpretation of her later heart disease is R.
Long-term systemic glucocorticoid treatment for sarcoidosis, with bone, glucose, blood pressure, infection and eye risks to manage
Dual-chamber implantable cardioverter-defibrillator, placed after sustained monomorphic ventricular tachycardia was induced at electrophysiology study; remote monitoring
S — Synthetic device status after the synthetic implant.

list.item:
Acute viral laryngitis (J04.0). Laryngitis after a viral cold, in a singer who has been singing hard; rapid influenza and COVID-19 tests are negative, there is no fever, the chest is clear and there is no thrush, so this needs no antibiotic and no change in her sarcoidosis treatment. Laryngeal sarcoidosis is possible but unlikely with a short illness after a cold; if the hoarseness lasts more than four weeks she needs laryngoscopy, as the hoarseness guideline advises. Singing on an inflamed larynx risks vocal fold injury, and she agreed to postpone Friday's concert. [S]
Voice rest for five days: no singing and quiet speech only; no whispering.
Warm fluids, steam inhalation and humidified air; throat lozenges.
Postpone Friday's concert; a letter for the promoter, with her consent, giving no medical details.
Continue prednisone 20 mg, methotrexate and atovaquone; call at once for fever of 38.0 °C or more, breathlessness or chest pain, because she is immunosuppressed.
Laryngoscopy with an ear, nose and throat specialist if the hoarseness lasts beyond four weeks.

Cardiac sarcoidosis with a defibrillator (D86.85). No palpitations or shocks; regular rhythm. [S]
Continue metoprolol and remote monitoring.

text.paragraph: Guideline basis: Baughman RP, et al. ERS clinical practice guidelines on treatment of sarcoidosis. Eur Respir J 2021;58(6):2004079 (PMID 34140301) (2021); Stachler RJ, et al. Clinical Practice Guideline: Hoarseness (Dysphonia) (Update). Otolaryngol Head Neck Surg 2018;158(1_suppl):S1-S42 (PMID 29494321) (2018)

Follow-up: Phone check in three days. Return if hoarseness lasts beyond four weeks or for fever, breathlessness or chest pain. Next planned review in August with the repeat FDG-PET. Next scheduled visit 2026-08-24: six months of treatment: repeat FDG-PET, steroid taper, and plans for touring. [S]
